title: Air France Flight 447: pitot icing, erroneous speed, stall, man-machine interaction, and status-discipline rail
summary: AF447 is encoded as a flight-deck state-legibility and man-machine interaction record: unreliable airspeed indications and a high-altitude stall trajectory are kept separate from later legal status and from any simplistic crew-blame frame.

status_history.note: Added as rev0027 flight-deck state / CRM rail lane record.

claims.claim: BEA’s public communications around AF447 warned against hasty interpretation from partial or non-validated information and created a human-factors working group to examine man-machine interactions and crew actions before final recommendations.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

type_payload.system: Airbus A330 flight deck, air-data sensing, autopilot/flight-control/crew response in high-altitude cruise
sequence_of_events: Pitot probe icing and erroneous speed indications; loss/degradation of automation/air-data reliability; aircraft entered and remained in stall; collision with ocean surface.
type_payload.proximate_cause: loss of control in flight after unreliable speed/state information and stall trajectory
contributing_factors: crew action interpretation requires careful official-report extraction
latent_conditions: need for disciplined safety-investigation status rather than early speculation
possible divergence between technical safety investigation and legal blame proceedings
training/procedure/automation-interface correction surfaces require second-pass extraction

follow_through: AF447 current legal status requires official/judicial source acquisition separate from BEA safety-causal record.

handling_notes: Aviation records must preserve the dignity of passengers, crew, families, responders, and survivors.
Do not flatten human-factors findings into pilot blame; separate physical system state, displayed state, automation mode, training, procedures, supervision, fatigue, and investigation/legal status.
This is historical/evidentiary infrastructure, not operational flight-safety guidance or legal advice.

unknowns: Full BEA final-report extraction was not performed in this pass; official page excerpts support bounded status and mechanism claims.
Current legal developments exist and need an official/judicial source-acquisition pass before being encoded as legal-status claims.
